newsitem.title: USA: Emerging market debt ends sharply higher.
newsitem.headline: Emerging market debt ends sharply higher.

text.p: A strong rally in the U.S. Treasury and stock market following lower-than-expected U.S. inflation data sent Brady bonds sharply higher but emerging market experts said volatility is expected to continue.

"The market rallied on the CPI (consumer price index)," said one trader at a European bank. "We saw some decent buying from clients for the first time in a while but I still think the market is heavy and I still think there is excess paper out there and dealers use this (environment) to sell."
Still, emerging market debt rose sharply allowing for a significant tightening of spreads on most credits.
"It's been down, boring and depressing for so long it is nice to have some refreshing news," said Dan Peirce, chief strategist of emerging market research at BankBoston Corp.
Earlier today, the U.S. Labor Department reported that the CPI rose 0.1 percent with the core rate, excluding volatile food and energy prices up 0.2 percent.
The tame inflation report sparked a strong rally in the U.S. Treasury market, with its benchmark 30-year U.S. Treasury bond closing up 29/32 at 94-07/32 to yield 7.09 percent.
The CPI data also helped to push the Dow Jones Industrial Average up 135 points to close unoffically at 6587.
Market experts said the rallies in both those markets spilled over into the emerging markets, which lead to strong price gains across the baord.

They noted, however, that higher yielding assets of countries such as Bulgaria and Ecuador outperformed the broader market with yield spreads tightening between 20 to 30 basis points against U.S. Treasuries.
"The markets that suffered a lot are doing a lot better," Peirce said, adding that spreads on Bulgarian debt continued to narrow due to a favorable market environment and positive fundamental news.
On Friday, the International Monetary Fund (IMF) approved a $657 million package of credits for Bulgaria to support the country's move toward a market economy.
On a price basis, Bulgarian FLRBs rose 1-5/8 to 43-1/2 bid and the country's IAB's jumped 1-5/8 to 59 bid.

"Positive fundmantal news coupled with the fact we are not in a defensive market environment at least not today and you get an extra kick," said another market source, referring to the Bulgaria's sharp price gains.
Trading sources said Ecuador also posted strong gains with the country's PDI bonds rising 1-1/4 to 55-1/2 bid and its discount bonds firming one percentage point to 64-1/4 bid.
In the broader emerging debt market, traders said spreads tightened by about five to 10 basis points.
Among the major Latin Bradys, market experts said Venezuelan pars rose 1-3/8 to 70 bid, Mexican pars firmed 7/8 bid to 70-5/8 bid and Argentine pars climbed 7/8 to 62 bid.
